newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: BPI still on lookout for merger prospects.
newsitem.headline: BPI still on lookout for merger prospects.

text.p: Bank of the Philippine Islands (BPI) is still on the lookout for merger opportunities, but BPI vice chairman Jaime Augusto Zobel de Ayala said on Monday it has to first "digest" the acquisition of CityTrust Banking Corp.
"We are always looking for acquisition opportunities. However, we need to digest CityTrust properly first," Ayala said in an interview with Reuters.
BPI has a tradition of acquiring smaller banks as part of its growth strategy.
BPI bought into CityTrust last year and the two banks posted a merged net income of 3.992 billion pesos in 1996 against BPI's 1.986 billion pesos and CityTrust's 959.9 million pesos in 1995.
Ayala said BPI's income would grow faster in the coming years since the merged bank would have a stronghold on the consumer banking business.
"Our consumer banking business is really going to take off with this merger," he said.

Ayala said he expected BPI to equal its sister firm, real estate giant Ayala Land Inc, in terms of contribution to its parent firm's bottomline. BPI is the banking subsidiary of conglomerate Ayala Corp, of which Jaime Ayala is the president.

Ayala Land has been the biggest contributor to Ayala Inc's net profit. Ayala said it contributed 60 percent of the conglomerate's net income in 1996, which analysts have estimated at about 5.56 billion pesos.
